settings.tv.confirmDeleteBroadcast: Delete broadcast "{name}"? Any active stream will be cut off.
settings.tv.mapped: Mapped — refresh the EPG source to fill in programs
settings.tv.sourceRequired: Source URL or path is required
settings.tv.confirmDeleteEpg: Delete EPG source "{name}"? Already-ingested programs stay until they expire.
settings.tv.noDevicesFound: No HDHomeRun devices found on the local network
settings.tv.prefilled: Form pre-filled — click "Add tuner" to save
settings.tv.confirmDeleteTuner: Delete tuner "{name}"? This removes all its channels and EPG data.
settings.tv.broadcastsHint: Go live from OBS, ffmpeg, or any RTMP encoder. Create a broadcast, point your encoder at the ingest URL with the stream key, and it appears as a Live TV channel — viewable in the browser and recordable by the DVR.
settings.tv.rtmpDisabled: RTMP ingest is disabled on this server. Set {env} and ensure the RTMP port (default {port}) is reachable.
settings.tv.noBroadcasts: No broadcasts yet. Create one below to go live.
settings.tv.tunersHint: Live TV pulls channels from network-attached tuners (HDHomeRun) and IPTV playlists (M3U). Each tuner is scanned automatically when added.
settings.tv.addTunerHint: HDHomeRun: enter the device's IP or full URL — discovery runs immediately. M3U: paste a playlist URL or absolute file path; some IPTV providers gate on a custom User-Agent.
settings.tv.discoverHint: Broadcasts a UDP query on your local network.
settings.tv.unmappedHint: These channels have no EPG mapping — they show up in the guide with no "now playing" info. Auto-match checks lcn → number and display-name → callsign; pick a source ID manually for anything auto-match missed.
settings.tv.epgHint: Pulls program data (titles, descriptions, schedules) from XMLTV feeds. Channels are auto-matched by lcn → channel number, falling back to display-name → callsign. Schedules Direct support coming later.
settings.tv.noEpg: No EPG sources configured yet — the guide will be empty.
settings.tv.channelsHint: Reorder channels or hide ones you don't watch from the guide. Hidden channels stay mapped and ingested; they just don't appear in the grid or now/next strip.
settings.arr.intro: Configure Radarr/Sonarr instances for the request workflow. Multiple instances per kind are supported — set one as default per kind, and use the additional instances for things like a separate 4K Radarr or alternate language Sonarr.
settings.arr.name: Name
settings.arr.noneAdminPicks: (none — admin will pick at approval time)
settings.arr.emptySub: Add a Radarr or Sonarr instance to enable the request workflow's auto-dispatch.
settings.arr.deleteWarn: In-flight requests routed to this service will lose their service binding.
settings.plugins.roleNotificationHint: Receives playback (play / pause / resume / stop / scrobble) and library.scan.complete events. Fire-and-forget: the result is ignored.
settings.plugins.roleMetadataHint: Called for each item during enrichment, after TMDB, TVDB, AniList and MusicBrainz, with its type, title, year, provider IDs and file name. It may return title, summary, tagline, genres, year, rating, release date, poster_url and provider IDs. By default those fill only empty fields; mode "override" replaces them. Locked fields are never changed, and provider IDs and posters are only filled.
settings.plugins.roleMetadataSummary: Fills or overrides unlocked metadata during enrichment
settings.plugins.roleTaskHint: Runs as a scheduled task — daily at 04:30 until you change it in Settings → Tasks — and receives the server version and the library list (no paths or keys). The text it returns becomes the run output; an error result fails the run.
settings.plugins.roleTaskSummary: Runs on its schedule in Settings → Tasks
settings.plugins.reachableGeneric: Plugin is reachable and advertises its tool
settings.plugins.intro: Plugins are external MCP servers OnScreen calls out to. Endpoints must speak Streamable HTTP and expose the tool for their role: {notify}, {enrich} or {task}.
settings.plugins.name: Name
settings.plugins.endpointHint: Full URL to the plugin's Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint.
settings.plugins.hostsHint: Extra hostnames this plugin may contact, one per line or comma-separated. The endpoint's own host is always allowed. Private/loopback IPs are always blocked.
settings.plugins.emptySub: Plugins extend OnScreen with external MCP servers for notifications and automation.
settings.storage.title: Media storage
settings.storage.hint: Where OnScreen reads media bytes from. {local} is the default and serves files straight from the filesystem. {s3} (AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Cloudflare R2) lets workers and clients read source and segments directly from the bucket or a CDN — taking byte delivery off this server. Leaving this disabled keeps the existing local-disk behaviour unchanged.
settings.storage.keyHint: The object key is a file's path with {mediaRoot} stripped and {pathPrefix} prepended. With a {cdn}, signed URLs point at the CDN (front a public-read bucket, or give the CDN origin credentials); otherwise OnScreen issues time-limited presigned bucket URLs.
settings.storage.mappingsHint: For active/passive disaster recovery: when this server is a standby whose Postgres is replicated from another site, the database holds the primary's absolute file paths. Map the primary's path prefix to this machine's mount so playback resolves locally. One {format} per line; leave empty on a primary/single-site server. Applies to the local-disk backend.
settings.webhooks.secretHint: Used to sign payloads with HMAC-SHA256. The signature is sent in the {header} header.
settings.webhooks.emptySub: Webhooks send HTTP POST notifications when media events occur in OnScreen.
settings.notifications.blurbDiscord: Post to a channel through a webhook.
settings.notifications.blurbTelegram: Message a group or channel through your bot.
settings.notifications.blurbNtfy: Push to phones via ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server.
settings.notifications.blurbGotify: Push to your self-hosted Gotify server.
settings.notifications.blurbEmail: Email a list of addresses using the server’s SMTP settings.
settings.notifications.secretDiscordHint: Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy Webhook URL. Treated as a secret.
settings.notifications.secretTelegramHin: From {bot}. Add the bot to your group first.
settings.notifications.secretNtfyHint: Only needed when the topic is protected.
settings.notifications.secretGotifyHint: Gotify → Apps → create an application and copy its token.
settings.notifications.reenterSecret: Re-enter the {field} when changing the server URL
settings.notifications.reenterToken: Re-enter the token when changing the server URL
settings.notifications.testSent: Test message sent — check the channel.
settings.notifications.testUndelivered: The test message could not be delivered.
settings.notifications.intro: Send request, problem-report and server alerts to a Discord channel, a Telegram group, an ntfy topic, a Gotify server or an email list. Every event is sent once per channel — not once per user. Links point at the Public URL from Settings → General; without one, messages carry no link.
settings.notifications.name: Name
settings.notifications.chatIdHint: Group IDs start with a minus sign. Add the bot to the group before sending a test.
settings.notifications.topicHint: On the public ntfy.sh anyone who knows the topic can read it — pick something hard to guess, or use a token.
settings.notifications.recipientsHint: Up to {max} addresses. Sent with the SMTP settings under Users → Email.
settings.notifications.allowPrivateHint: For a {kind} server on your LAN or this machine (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, localhost). Leave off for a public server — OnScreen then refuses to send anywhere private.
settings.notifications.emptySub: Add one above to get request and server alerts where your household already chats.
settings.backup.finishedWithErrors: Restore finished with errors — review the output below
settings.backup.migrationsFailedToast: Restore succeeded but post-restore migrations failed — review below
settings.backup.completeMigrated: Restore complete; schema migrated forward to v{version}.
settings.backup.complete: Restore complete. You may need to sign in again.
settings.backup.backupHint: Downloads a Postgres custom-format dump of everything OnScreen tracks — users, libraries, items, watch history, credits, playlists. Media files and artwork live on disk and are not included; they are rebuilt from the scan sources. The filename includes the current schema version ({suffix}) so future restores know whether the dump is compatible with the running build.
settings.backup.restoreHint: Upload a backup produced by this page. The existing database is {wiped} and replaced. If the dump is from an older schema, the server runs migrations after the restore so it ends up matching this build. Dumps from a {newer} server are refused unless you explicitly override.
settings.backup.passwordSso: (leave blank if you sign in via SSO)
settings.backup.mismatch: Schema mismatch — dump is {dump}, server expects {server}.
settings.backup.mismatchHint: Restoring would leave the server unable to read columns it expects to find. Upgrade the server build, or override only if you know the schema gap is benign.
settings.observability.saved: Tracing settings saved — restart the server for changes to take effect
settings.observability.title: OpenTelemetry Tracing
settings.observability.hint: Exports distributed traces over OTLP/gRPC. Tracing is wired throughout the server (HTTP routes, DB queries, scanner, transcode); when disabled, instrumentation is a no-op and emits zero traces.
settings.observability.restartHint: The tracer provider is built once at process start. Save here, then restart the server (and any worker binaries) for new settings to take effect.
settings.observability.endpointHint: Must include scheme ({http} or {https}); TLS is enabled automatically for {scheme}.
settings.observability.sampleHint: 0.0–1.0. {one} samples every trace (dev default); production with a paid backend often runs 0.05–0.1.
settings.observability.jaegerHint: The bundled docker compose ships a Jaeger all-in-one under the {profile} profile:
settings.observability.jaegerUi: UI at {url}. OTLP/gRPC listens on {port} — drop that into the endpoint above.
settings.nodes.saved: Saved {node} — restart that node to apply
settings.nodes.confirmRemove: Remove saved config for "{node}"? It reverts to env defaults; an online node stays in the list.
settings.nodes.notice: Per-node configuration. Unlike System settings (which every node shares), each node reads only its own row, so these are safe to set per machine. {restart} If a bad bind address locks a node out, set {ignore} in its environment to boot from env only. The bootstrap set ({db}, {secret}, {node}) must stay in the environment — it's needed before this table is reachable.
settings.nodes.noticeRestart: Restart the target node to apply.
settings.nodes.bindHint: You're connected through the API address — changing it needs a matching restart and reconnect.
settings.nodes.disableWorker: Disable the in-process transcode worker on this node
settings.nodes.removeTitle: Delete this node's saved config (e.g. a decommissioned node). It reverts to env defaults; an online node stays in the list.
settings.remote.loadFailed: Failed to load remote access settings
settings.remote.savedOn: Saved — the router mapping follows within a few seconds
settings.remote.savedOff: Saved — the router mapping is removed
settings.remote.unavailable: Remote access is not available on this server.
settings.remote.dangerTitle: This opens your server to the internet.
settings.remote.dangerIntro: With port mapping on, anyone who finds your address can reach the OnScreen sign-in page. Before you turn it on:
settings.remote.dangerHttps: Serve HTTPS — upload a certificate in {link}, or put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front.
settings.remote.plainHttp: This server serves plain HTTP now: passwords and tokens would cross the internet unencrypted.
settings.remote.danger2fa: Turn on two-factor sign-in for every admin ({link}).
settings.remote.no2fa: Your account doesn't have it yet.
settings.remote.dangerPasswords: Use strong passwords for every account, and remove accounts nobody uses.
settings.remote.dangerVpn: A VPN such as Tailscale reaches the server from outside without opening a port at all.
settings.remote.mappingHint: The server asks your router (UPnP IGD, PCP or NAT-PMP) to forward a public port to its own port {port}, renews the lease while it runs, and removes it when you turn this off or the server stops. Only one node of a cluster maps. Your router must allow UPnP or NAT-PMP; in Docker the server needs host networking to reach it.
settings.remote.loopback: The server listens on {addr} — loopback only — so no other device can reach it and nothing will be mapped. Change the listen address in {link} first.
settings.remote.mapPort: Map a port on my router automatically
settings.remote.externalPortHint: — empty = the same as the listen port ({port})
settings.remote.permanent: Permanent (the router doesn't time leases out; re-checked every {minutes} minutes)
settings.system.saved: System settings saved — restart the server to apply
settings.system.notice: These were previously environment variables and are read at startup — {restart}. Node- and site-specific settings (connection strings, secret key, bind addresses, file paths, site ID, per-worker hardware) stay in the environment by design.
settings.system.noticeRestart: restart the server to apply changes
settings.system.deliveryHint: Object storage itself is configured under Integrations ▸ Storage.
settings.system.publicCacheHint: — for a CDN fronting the app (local-disk deployments)
settings.system.staticAbrHint: — pre-encode popular titles' ladders to the store (object storage + CDN recommended)
settings.system.scannerHint: Library scan parallelism and how long a vanished file waits before it's marked gone.
settings.system.discoveryHint: Whether the server advertises itself over UDP broadcast so first-party clients can auto-find it.
settings.libraryHealth.regrabHasFile: {app} still has a file for it, so only an upgrade will be grabbed — delete the file in {app} for a same-quality replacement.
settings.libraryHealth.noteBlocklisted: Blocklisted the bad release and requested a new download.
settings.libraryHealth.notManaged: No Radarr/Sonarr instance manages this title.
settings.libraryHealth.loadMoreDamagedFa: Failed to load more damaged files
settings.libraryHealth.resolvedToast: Report resolved — the reporter was notified.
settings.libraryHealth.regrabNotResolved: Re-grab requested, but the report couldn't be resolved: {error}
settings.libraryHealth.intro: Problems users reported with "Report a problem", files the integrity check found damaged, and titles that still need a match or a poster. Resolving or dismissing a report tells the person who filed it.
settings.libraryHealth.noOpen: No open reports. Nothing to do here.
settings.libraryHealth.regrabTitle: Ask Radarr/Sonarr to search again, then resolve this report
settings.libraryHealth.damagedHint: Found by the integrity check task (Settings ▸ Tasks). These files fail to decode past a point and won't play. Re-grab asks Radarr/Sonarr for a new copy.
settings.import.intro: Bring each user's watched state, resume points, ratings, favorites, playlists and play history over from a Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server. Items are matched by file path, then by TMDB, TVDB or IMDb ID, so add your libraries here and scan them first. Preview to see what matches before anything is written; running an import again adds only what's new, and anything users already did on OnScreen is kept.
settings.import.notStored: It's used for this import only and isn't stored.
settings.import.accountsSub_one: {server} · {count} account. Choose the OnScreen user each one's history goes to.
settings.import.accountsSub_other: {server} · {count} accounts. Choose the OnScreen user each one's history goes to.
settings.import.historyOnlyTitle: Plex shows this account's play history, not its resume points, ratings or playlists
settings.import.plexNote: Plex shows resume points, ratings and playlists only for the server owner's account (the token's). The other accounts bring their play history and what it shows they watched.
settings.import.historyNote: Play history counts toward play counts, Trending and analytics. Plays older than the server's watch-history retention are left out, as they'd be removed anyway (the items still count as watched).
settings.import.noPlayLog: {server} keeps no log of individual plays, so each watched item brings one play, on the date it was last played. A playlist shared with everyone comes over for each user who could see it.
settings.import.outsideRetention_one: {count} play was older than the history retention.
settings.import.outsideRetention_other: {count} plays were older than the history retention.
settings.security.tlsSaved: TLS certificate saved — restart to serve HTTPS
settings.security.tlsCleared: TLS certificate cleared — restart to apply
settings.security.title: Security
settings.security.devicesHint: Browsers and apps signed in to your account. Signing one out ends its session at once; your other devices stay signed in.
settings.security.revokeAllConfirm: Sign out every other device signed in to your account? This browser stays signed in.
settings.security.apiKeysHint: Your long-lived keys for scripts and integrations (Home Assistant, Kometa). A key acts as you, but can't sign in or change account security. See {doc} for usage.
settings.security.allApiKeysHint: Every user's API keys. Revoke one that is leaked or no longer needed; it stops working on its next request.
settings.security.tlsHint: Serve HTTPS directly without a reverse proxy. The key is stored encrypted and loaded into memory at startup — no cert file on disk. Restart-required. For per-host certs in a cluster, use a reverse proxy or the {env} env path instead.
settings.security.tlsEnv: TLS is configured via {cert} / {key}. Unset those env vars to manage the certificate here.
settings.security.servingForExpires: Serving an uploaded certificate for {subject} — expires {date}.
settings.maintenance.title: Re-probe technical metadata
settings.maintenance.hint: Re-runs {tool} on existing files to backfill technical metadata that older scans didn't persist — notably {fps} (which the adaptive-bitrate ladder needs to align segments) and audio {rg} tags. It clears the scanner's content hashes so the next scan can't fast-skip unchanged files, then queues that scan; the re-probe runs in the background. Safe to run anytime — it doesn't change your files, only re-reads them.
settings.maintenance.subtle: This covers probe-derived fields only. Missing posters and TMDB ratings come from metadata enrichment — use {setPoster} or {fixMatch} for those.
settings.maintenance.running: The re-probe is running in the background. Check {tasks} or the server logs for scan progress.
settings.email.smtpHint: Outbound email for password resets and invitations. Without SMTP, admins must hand out invite URLs manually and the "Forgot password" flow is disabled.
settings.email.testHint: Sends a one-off SMTP test using the saved configuration above — handy for verifying credentials before relying on password reset.
settings.unmatched.title: Fix Match
settings.unmatched.intro: Items the scanner couldn't auto-match against TMDB. Pick the right result to attach IDs and pull metadata + artwork. The match also merges into an existing canonical row if you pick a TMDB ID that another item in the library already uses.
settings.unmatched.empty: All movies and shows are matched. Nothing to do here.
settings.unmatched.yearTitle: Release year filter — clear to search all years
settings.unmatched.noResults: No results — try a different query.
settings.missingArt.intro: Items the auto-fetcher couldn't pull a poster for. Pick a TMDB variant or paste a URL pointing to any image (jpg / png / webp). The image is downloaded and written next to the item's media files.
settings.missingArt.empty: All items have posters. Nothing to do here.
settings.missingArt.noPosters: TMDB has no posters for this title.
settings.missingArt.noTmdbId: No TMDB ID attached — paste a URL below.
settings.missingArt.pasteHint: Must be a direct link to the image file (right-click → Copy image address). Page URLs from IMDB, Wikipedia, Google Images won't work.
